title: Linear maps out of finite-dimensional spaces are continuous
statement: Let $E$ be a field with an absolute value $|\cdot|$ that is nontrivial (some $x\in E$ has $|x|\notin\{0,1\}$) and for which $E$ is complete; for instance a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its absolute value $|\cdot|_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. A *topological $E$-vector space* is an $E$-vector space with a topology for which addition $V\times V\to V$, negation and scalar multiplication $E\times V\to V$ are continuous. If $V$ is a finite-dimensional Hausdorff topological $E$-vector space and $W$ is any topological $E$-vector space, then every $E$-linear map $V\to W$ is continuous.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, proof, p. 60; the finite-dimensional topological linear algebra used in the sentence that the representation category admits kernels and cokernels.
